questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the particles in a liquid?

options.text: Closely packed in a regular pattern, vibrating in fixed positions
Close together but irregularly arranged, able to move around each other
Far apart and moving randomly at high speeds
Fixed in position with no movement at all

questions.explanation: In a liquid, particles are close together but not in a regular arrangement. They can move around each other, which is why liquids can flow and take the shape of their container while maintaining a fixed volume.

questions.stem: A gas has no fixed shape and no fixed volume because its particles:

options.text: Are held together by strong forces of attraction
Are far apart with negligible forces between them and move randomly at high speeds
Are closely packed and slide past each other

questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with negligible forces of attraction between them. They move randomly at high speeds in all directions, which means a gas has no fixed shape and will expand to fill any container.
